newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan needs debate on use of public money - banker.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs debate on use of public money - banker.

text.p: The chairman of the Regional Banks Association of Japan, Takashi Tamaki, said on Wednesday that the issue of using public money to protect depositors from banks' financial difficulties should be debated in Japan.

Tamaki, who is also president of Chiba Bank Ltd, told a news conference that in his personal opinion, the collapse of more Japanese financial institutions was inevitable in the process of Japan's "Big Bang" financial deregulation.
He said the use of public money to protect depositors should be debated as an option to cope with such a situation.
"Without considering the use of public money, it will be difficult to cope with the Big Bang," he said.
Tamaki also said that he welcomed Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's recent comment that his ministry would firmly support Japan's top 20 banks in their effort to resolve their bad-loan problems.
It would be a good thing both at home and abroad if Japanese authorities showed their resolve to support the nation's big banks, he said.
